text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Sharp American criticism of Israel's settlement policies and attempts in the Knesset to remove Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu from power.
- Government is keen to preserve workers' rights within the framework of the economic privatisation programme.
- President Hosni Mubarak sends a letter to France's Jacques Chirac on the stalemate in the peace process.
- The General Authority for Investment says Egypt is the world's third most attractive country to foreign investment.
- Cabinet approves setting up 12 touristic projects with a total cost of 225 million pounds ($66 million).

- Unified labour law to be discussed by the cabinet. Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri tells the labour union that workers are the basis of development and the springboard for advances in all fields. Guarantees for workers' rights.
- Egypt to set up seven free trade zones in 1997.
- Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says in Paris that Israel's settlement policy is dangerous.
- Unified labour law to be drafted by parliament during the current session.
- Greek president to visit Egypt on Saturday.
